newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's Telstra hands over radar deal.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's Telstra hands over radar deal.

text.p: The Australian government on Wednesday approved a plan for Lockheed Martin Corp and the unlisted Transfield Defence Systems to take over management of the troubled A$1 billion over-the-horizon radar project from state telecoms giant Telstra Corp.
"A heads of agreement was signed this morning giving Commonwealth approval for new arrangements of the Jindalee Over the Horizon radar project," Defence Minister Ian McLachlan told parliament.

Lockheed and Transfield will form a joint venture to manage the Jindalee Operational Network (JORN) radar project and would acquire a Telstra unit called Telstar, which is a key contractor in the project.
Lockheed currently owns 40 percent of Telstar and would have a 50 percent stake in the joint venture. Transfield would hold the remaining 50 percent.
McLachlan said the change would take effect from February 17. He did not disclose the terms of the deal.
"Also as part of those new arrangements ... the progress payment mechanism will be changed from the present milestone system to one which is predominantly based on earned value," he said.
McLachlan said the new payment system, which he did not detail further, would encourage early delivery of the already-delayed JORN.
The system, aimed at providing radar coverage across Australia's remote northern coastline, was due onstream by 1997 but had been delayed until at least the turn of the century.
McLachlan did not say when the system was now expected to be operational.
"This is a very important capability for Australia's defence and we welcome very much the involvement of two of the leading defence contractors," he said.
